public_prompt:
You control a finite-thickness paper simulator to follow an origami document. Image 1 is a document page (or YOUR requested crop); image 2 shows the ACTUAL current paper in three depth-rendered views: TOP (+z with the fixed board coordinate grid), OBLIQUE (+z), and BOTTOM OBLIQUE (-z underside view so lower-layer flaps are visible). Other pages are available. Read the task scope and numbered diagram instructions yourself. The system does NOT identify the next instruction or tell you when the work is complete.
Return ONE JSON action, no prose. Use the actual TOP view to place a straight crease in CURRENT WORLD/BOARD coordinates: x right, y up, 15cm equals 1 unit; an unrotated 15cm square has corners (0,0),(1,1); the supplied sheet may instead be a rectangle or hexagon, as shown; origin of rotations at board (0.5,0.5). A rotated paper can extend beyond [0,1], allowed [-0.5,1.5]. Diagram orientation may differ: explicitly rotate the paper when needed; NEVER renormalize the folded outline.
Actions:
{"op":"fold_line","line":[[x1,y1],[x2,y2]],"moving_point":[x,y],"layers":"all","sense":"toward","angle_deg":180}
line is the CREASE, NOT the arrow target. moving_point must lie on the moving flap. layers is all (every layer on that side), top (uppermost connected panel under the point), or bottom (lowest panel). toward lifts toward +z/the camera; away folds behind. Valley arrows normally use toward; mountain use away. Angle may be less than 180. Read arrow tail to head. Only straight creases already represented in the frozen mesh can execute; the current mesh hinge is fitted within a fixed 0.6mm geometric instrument band; no answer-aware snapping or measurement tool.
{"op":"unfold"} physically opens the latest active fold in forward time. Or {"op":"unfold","fold_id":3,"angle_deg":90} opens a specified active fold by a positive angle up to its remaining angle. Omitting angle opens it fully. Earlier folds can open while later, disjoint folds remain; overlapping dependent folds must open first, and physical contact may still block an independent fold. Partial unfolding retains the fold ID. This is NOT undo and preserves plastic history. Paper turns update the stored axes. Active fold IDs and their past commands are public.
{"op":"turn_over","axis":"y"} physically flips the entire paper 180 degrees around world x or y. {"op":"rotate_paper","degrees":90} physically rotates in the plane, positive counterclockwise.
{"op":"view_page","page":1,"crop":[0,0,1,1]} selects a 1-based page and optional normalized image rectangle (x right,y DOWN). This only changes document view; it does not change paper or advance any instruction.
{"op":"undo"} reverts your last accepted PAPER operation; it does NOT refund attempts, cost, or history. Document view changes do not enter the undo stack.
{"op":"finish"} ends whenever YOU judge the requested scope complete. Acceptance only means a motion executed; it never certifies diagram correctness. There is no automatic final-review hint.
Failed calls, navigation, undo and finish all consume attempts. All public attempt history follows. A failure leaves the paper unchanged only when rollback_verified is true. Do not repeat an unchanged rejected request without a reason. You may recover or change strategy. No private target/expected-step count is visible.
For a packet of multiple upper or lower layers use layers={"side":"top","count":2} or side="bottom" with a positive integer count. Layers are ordered at moving_point; choose a point through the intended packet. This moves exactly that many connected panels, and rejects if the point does not intersect enough layers. A diagram may call a folded packet a top flap or layer even when it contains multiple physical panels. Infer its packet size from the paper and past folds. Count is not inferred from the diagram by the simulator.
The task starts from an already prepared paper state. Its past preparation commands are disclosed and were executed physically; they are not your attempts. Begin at the requested diagram scope. Undo cannot go before this starting state. You may physically unfold a preparation fold. Remaining angles and IDs describe past actions, not private goals. No future reference actions are exposed.
Follow the explicit task scope and completion rules. By default, follow illustrated intermediate states in order as well as the final shape. If the task explicitly permits equivalent action orders or moving halves, that permission takes precedence. Required fold-and-open operations must still be physically completed; an unfolded outline alone does not prove that precreases were made. The private shape checks and their progress are never shown during the episode.
Public controller capability: each rotation is discretized to at most 600 integration frames, with at most 0.5 degree rotation and 0.8 mm outer-grip arc travel per frame. Thus a 180 degree rotation of a moving region whose farthest gripped point is more than about 153 mm from the axis can exceed this limit. A large complementary half may be unsupported even when the equivalent smaller moving half is supported. When the task permits equivalent halves, choose a supported one. A capability_limit rejection is an interface bound, consumes an attempt, and does not mean the intended crease is wrong. Physical contact can also reject otherwise valid intended folds. These bounds are shared by all tasks and models.
Paper views may expand to keep the actual paper visible. Read the TOP coordinate ticks: one board unit is always 15 cm, and coordinates are never renormalized to the visible outline. Only the view extent changes.
